no low-voltage ECG or ventricular wall thickening mentioned for amyloidosis
no description of absent P waves or fibrillatory waves on the first ECG
response.rationale: R3 is the strongest composite candidate because the raw spans show biatrial dilatation plus grade III diastolic dysfunction, together indicating a restrictive/infiltrative cardiac process. The prominent y descent, though cited by R4, better fits restrictive physiology than tamponade. R1 merely restates the diastolic dysfunction without accounting for biatrial enlargement or arrhythmia. R2 is contradicted by the presence of discrete inverted P waves and an atrial rate of 210 bpm, which is not atrial fibrillation. R4 lacks the required pericardial effusion and tamponade physiology.

rejected.why: The raw ECG shows discrete inverted P waves with an atrial rate of 210 bpm, not the absent P waves and fibrillatory waves required for atrial fibrillation.
A prominent y descent is more consistent with restrictive/constrictive physiology than cardiac tamponade, and there is no pericardial effusion or right heart collapse described.
